A reflection across a line through the origin has matrix form  
\[
\begin{pmatrix}\cos 2\theta & \sin 2\theta\\ \sin 2\theta & -\cos 2\theta\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Given
\[
R\begin{pmatrix}5\\0\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix},
\]
we get
\[
5\begin{pmatrix}\cos 2\theta\\ \sin 2\theta\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}4\\3\end{pmatrix}.
\]
So
\[
\cos 2\theta=\frac45,\qquad \sin 2\theta=\frac35.
\]
Thus
\[
R=\begin{pmatrix}
\frac45 & \frac35\\[2mm]
\frac35 & -\frac45
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Now apply \(R\) to \(\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}\):
\[
R\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac45 & \frac35\\[2mm]
\frac35 & -\frac45
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}-2\\3\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
-\frac85+\frac95\\[2mm]
-\frac65-\frac{12}{5}
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac15\\[2mm]
-\frac{18}{5}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The answer is \(\begin{pmatrix}\frac15\\[2mm]-\frac{18}{5}\end{pmatrix}\).
